observations: Two car headlights are shown, wrapped in clear plastic film.
The headlights have a modern, multi-element design with LED daytime running lights.
The plastic film is visible on the outer casing and the front lens.
The interior of the headlight housing is not visible.
The background appears to be a workshop or storage area.

claims.evidence: The plastic film obscures the actual condition of the lens and housing; it may be used or have minor surface damage.

claims.claim: Original Toyota part, not China copy. No crack, all clips and brackets complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The plastic film may be thin or brittle, leading to cracks or peeling under stress.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the headlight without the plastic film.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged or peeling film

risks.risk: The internal LED or bulb may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the headlight powered on and producing a clear beam.

risks.risk: The headlight may be a generic or aftermarket part rather than an original Toyota part.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's label or part number on the headlight.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the headlight without the plastic film to check for cracks or damage.
Video of the headlight powered on and functioning.
Photo of the manufacturer's label or part number.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
